reason: Not refuted. This is an info-only 'stays closed' item, and its numbers reproduce exactly. I re-ran scratchpad recheck5_agg.py: 30 of 39 6bba clips and 0 of 17 44b6 clips have freezes (248 frozen transitions). Post-freeze GT edges: 2,066, FN 213 (10.31%), FP 242 (FP/TP 13.06%). Normal edges inside freeze clips: FN 4.53%, FP/TP 4.83%. Excess: FN 119.5, FP 152.5. Ceiling: 0.00625 pooled (GT 40,093) and 0.00680 per 6bba GT (36,900). recheck5b_out.json confirms the anatomy: both_linked 86 (median 7.05 um), one_free 49 (6.74 um), miss 72. About 73% of the excess FN is link-class and about 20% is misses. Post TP steps have a median of ~3.0 um against ~1.9 um on normal frames. Frozen GT steps have a median of 0, so the GT copies positions on frozen frames (CONTEXT l.22 'GT still moving' is wrong for the bulk of them). VALUE: the finding correctly claims no gain. Private upside of ~0..+0.001 with unknown sign is reasonable: the only measured geometric fixes were ~0 or net FP-positive (velocity carry; sqrt(k+1) gates +31 TP/+58 FP), and ILP-first is the in-sample channel that failed on the LB (probes 21/29/30). FEASIBILITY: 'no build, no probe' is trivially within R1-R10. Even a lab pass could not be adopted: if the public embryo has no freezes, R4 cannot see the change; even with freezes, capturing 0-30% of ~0.0068 is at most ~+0.002 at LB rounding; R8 ends new mechanisms at 27 Sep 12:00 UTC; and the finals slots are committed (K2 #37 / twin #38). Finals: every candidate (K2, twin, K1 exp58t, #34, and exp52, which is exp39-lineage without the edge filter) carries a post-freeze defect, so it cannot tell the finals apart. Two statements need correcting before the curator records the FACT. (1) The claim 'larger than the old base's +0.004, so the flow prior did NOT fix it' compares unlike numbers. The old +0.004 is exp39 AFTER the edge filter, pooled over 128,883 GT in 199 videos (~73% 6bba), which is ~0.0055 per 6bba GT. The right comparison for x138, which has no edge filter, is exp39 BEFORE the filter: 0.0089 pooled, ~0.012 per 6bba GT, post FP/TP 15% vs 4.6%. So x138 roughly halves the pre-filter excess but keeps ~2x normal error rates. 'Not fixed' holds; 'larger than before' does not. (2) 'There is no CPU replay' is too strong. It is true for a change inside motion_relink_edges. But the exp60 npz dumps hold presafe_* nodes and edges (with motion_relinked/edge_prob flags), and tools/trainlab.py replay(ns, dump, 'presafe') has kernel parity. So a post-relink geometric re-solve limited to post-freeze transitions CAN be replayed on CPU at the presafe slot, with gap closing already baked in. That matters for the post-deadline item and does not change the 29 Sep verdict.
fix: Record as the finding proposes (FACT, post-deadline linker item #1, private-risk note, no F1/F2 change), with two wording corrections. (a) Replace 'larger than the old base's +0.004, so the flow prior did NOT fix it' with: 'x138 (no edge filter) post-freeze excess is ~0.0068 per 6bba GT. exp39 was ~0.012 before the edge filter and ~0.0055 after it (old +0.004 pooled over 199 videos). So the x138 flow prior and tail roughly halve the pre-filter defect but leave ~2x normal FN and FP/TP rates on post-freeze transitions.' (b) Replace 'no CPU replay' with: 'an in-relink change is not replayable. A post-relink geometric re-solve limited to post-freeze transitions is replayable on CPU from the exp60 presafe dump (trainlab.replay start=presafe). That is the required lab hook for the post-deadline item. Use geometric or flow cost only; never ILP or edge-net trust.' Optional: fix CONTEXT l.22 'frozen frames with GT still moving' to 'GT positions copied on frozen frames (step median 0), so the post-freeze GT step is ~2 frames of motion'. No build, no probe, no slot.
